heading: Qwen3-32B neuron sides (positive/negative): ~90% one main job, ~7% two, ~2–4% not yet understood
definition: in Qwen3-32B about 90% of neuron poles have one main job, about 7% two related jobs and about 2–4% are not yet understood.
summary: Only the original essay reports these shares, from a preliminary audit that gives no sample size, method or error bar. No independent study has tested this split in Qwen3-32B, so the figures remain the author's estimates.

suggested_status.by_scale: R0 at 10-100B (Qwen3-32B, original essay only; counts: versions.V1.studies_by_size = {10-100B: 1}). No tests at toy, <1B, 1-10B or >100B. No test at a stated training stage: the original's Qwen3-32B stage is not stated (counts: versions.V1.studies_by_stage = {not stated: 1}). The nearest outside checks, arXiv:2511.06739 at 10-100B (Qwen-2.5-32B-Instruct) and arXiv:2602.20904 at 1-10B (two dense 7B models), count as V2 evidence only. They leave these V1 levels unchanged.
suggested_status.reason: The original essay is the only study that tests V1 (counts: versions.V1.studies_tested = 1; versions.V1.original_sources_linked = [TITLE:Neural Networks Are Already Clean]). No supports, limits_scope or challenges verdicts exist on V1 (counts: versions.V1.verdicts all 0). The shares are the author's estimates from a preliminary audit: roughly 90% one main job with small related offshoots, ~7% two related jobs, ~2-4% not yet understood (R1-R3). The text gives no sample size, method or error bar (problems line; counts: versions.V1.tested_with_uncertainty = 0, versions.V1.tested_with_code = 0). It also names no judge and no threshold for 'one thing', though the R1 note says the essay admits such thresholds matter. The essay's own held-out test (R4-R6) has controls (counts: versions.V1.tested_with_controls = 1): 76% of new examples fired strongly vs 11% for near misses and about 1% for distant concepts. It is limited to positive-side explanations and does not measure the job-count split. The nearest outside checks are V2 evidence, not V1 tests. arXiv:2511.06739 (V2 limits_scope) had gpt-5-mini sort the first 60 MLP neurons per layer of Qwen-2.5-32B-Instruct into three classes from top-64 activating contexts: 20.2% specific, 46.9% fuzzy/broad and 32.9% polysemantic (r4-r6, figure-only). Its verdict counts 67.1% as one consistent explanation. arXiv:2602.20904 (V2 supports) reports about 6.1% and 5.9% uninterpretable neurons in Qwen2.5-Math-7B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B. These figures come from the text (Fig. 7), not a row. Both studies judge whole neurons in other models, not Qwen3-32B poles, and neither reports a two-related-jobs share. Neither shares authors with an original, but the two share an author with each other (Jake Ward), so they are not two independent groups (author lists from candidates.csv). No other study in the packs reports a Qwen3-32B neuron or pole share. The level is provisional. The studies the reader marked as testing V1 but the verdict did not count (counts: versions.V1.reader_said_tested_verdict_did_not = 11) are in no pack, and the completeness critic found that no step has yet listed or re-verdicted them.
suggested_status.open_questions: Three results would change the level. (1) A pole-level audit by another group of Qwen3-32B or a similar model, or of Qwen3-32B with the original's method published, that states its sample size, its threshold for 'one thing', its judge and its error bars. If it found similar shares, that would point toward R2; if it found a much lower one-job share, toward C. An audit that shares authors with the original would count as R1, not R2. Whole-neuron shares on other models, such as arXiv:2511.06739 and arXiv:2602.20904, do not close this gap. (2) A simulation-scored held-out test on Qwen3-32B neurons that covers both poles. (3) A check of whether any of the studies the reader marked as testing V1, which the verdict did not count (counts: versions.V1.reader_said_tested_verdict_did_not = 11), report Qwen3-32B shares. This check has not been done. It needs a script to list these studies with their verdict reasons, a new verdict on any that report a neuron or pole job share, Qwen-family results or MoE shares, and a rebuilt V1 pack. Any independent pole-level or Qwen3-32B share audit among the reads could be in this set.

original_result.setup: In a preliminary audit, AI agents wrote explanations for the positive and negative sides of Qwen3-32B neurons, but the essay does not describe how the audit was done.
original_result.result: Roughly 90% of neuron sides had one main job, often with small related offshoots; about 7% had two related jobs, and about 2–4% were not yet understood. A separate test on 183 neurons from the essay's gallery of examples, using explanations of their positive side, found that 76% of new examples fired the neuron strongly versus 11% of near misses, but it does not measure this split.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

wording_issues.phrase: about 90% of neuron poles have one main job
wording_issues.issue: The source row gives 'roughly 90%, often with small related offshoots'. The note says it is the author's estimate from a preliminary audit and admits that thresholds for 'one thing' matter. The statement drops both the offshoots qualifier and the framing as a preliminary estimate. The problems line says the text gives no sample size, method or error bar.

The only quantitative held-out test in the essay measures something else. On 183 of 200 random gallery neurons with positive-side explanations, 76% of new examples written from the explanation fired the neuron strongly, and the explanation beat its near misses for 164 neurons. Near misses fired strongly 11% of the time. Distant concepts fired about 1% of the time, and 179 of 183 neurons never fired on them. This is a per-example firing rate on positive sides, not a share of poles with one job. A verdict fix says R4 also bears on V6.

wording_issues.phrase: about 7% two related jobs and about 2–4% are not yet understood
wording_issues.issue: Rows give ~7% and ~2-4% with baseline 'not stated' and the note 'Original claim value'. The text describes no method for sorting poles into these categories.

method_sensitivity.factor: Threshold for counting a pole as doing 'one thing' (for example, lumping closely related idioms together)
method_sensitivity.what: The essay itself says the percentages depend on where this threshold is set. The rows give no figures for alternative thresholds, so the size of the effect is not shown.

method_sensitivity.factor: Explaining from top-k activating examples only
method_sensitivity.what: The essay says top-k examples alone can mislead, and gives four examples. (1) The negative pole was ignored, so the Santa graph neurons were labelled 'capital cities'. (2) The context was too short, so long-context neurons looked polysemantic. (3) The SwiGLU double-negative sign regime put a sign-flipped leak (Colossians) at the top of the list. (4) Commas were summary sites, so the Colorado neuron looked like a 'comma neuron'. The essay's own check writes new examples, near misses and distant concepts from each explanation (R4-R6). The rows give no V1 share measured with top-k inspection alone, so they can't show how much the split would change.

status_amendment.public_note: This entry now notes that the closest outside studies, on other Qwen models, measure whole neurons rather than neuron poles, so they count only for the version about other models, and that a set of possibly relevant studies has not yet been checked. The level is unchanged: only the original essay tests the 90% / 7% / 2–4% split.
